citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
A female tan mini goldendoodle, date of birth 10/21/18 with ID tag number 017 had a health condition requiring treatment
in consultation with the attending veterinarian. There was moderate buildup of hard brown material on the surface of the
cheek teeth especially along the upper part of the teeth near the gum line. The gums did not appear red or swollen and
the dog was in good body condition. The physical exam records for the dog from 7/9/26 include the finding "severe dental
tartar" by the attending veterinarian with a recommendation for dental scaling. The licensee stated he had scaled the teeth
but stated he may have only cleaned the front teeth. On today's inspection, the cheek teeth still appeared in need of
cleaning.
The abnormal build-up of material on the teeth can cause damage to the gum tissue and tooth structures. This condition
could be painful, may decrease the dog's ability to eat normally, and may result in spread of bacteria to other parts of the
body such as liver and kidneys which can negatively impact the overall health of the animal.
The licensee must ensure dogs with health conditions such as dental disease are treated according to the attending
veterinarian's recommendations.
Correct by: November 2, 2026

There was no written contingency plan on file at the facility.
Failure to have a written contingency plan can result in lack of readiness for emergencies or disasters.
Facilities must develop, document, and follow an appropriate plan to provide for the humane handling, treatment,
transportation, housing, and care of their animals in the event of an emergency or disaster.

There were no heartworm testing records available. The licensee could not recall if the testing had been performed and
he just didn't have the records on file or if the testing had not been performed. The Program of Veterinary Care (PVC)
states heartworm testing will be performed annually on 3 dogs.
Failure to follow sampling requirements in the PVC or to maintain testing records can lead to failure to detect or treat
disease in the dogs.
The facility must follow the Program of Veterinary Care including sampling for parasites including heartworm and must
maintain records with results of testing.
Correct by: December 21, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
